confirmed.title: OfflineQueue.flush is re-entrant: concurrent flushes double-send, drop an unexecuted item, and can crash on items[0]
confirmed.detail: `flush` is an actor method that suspends on `await executor.execute(item)`. Swift actors are re-entrant at suspension points, and the app calls flush from several places at once (Features/RootView.swift:36 `.task { flushOfflineQueue() }`, RootView.swift:56 on network reconnect, ShoppingView.swift:118 on every shopping reload, SavedView.swift:139 on saved reload). Scenario with queue [item1, item2]: flush A reads `items.first` = item1 and suspends in execute; flush B enters, also reads item1 and executes it again; A resumes and `items.removeFirst()` removes item1; B resumes and `items.removeFirst()` removes item2, which was never sent — a queued Saved/purchase operation is silently lost (result.sent is even incremented for it). Variant with a single-item queue: A succeeds and removes item1 (queue now empty); B's execute fails with a transient error and runs `items[0].attempts += 1` on an empty array → index out of range trap. The 'replay order preserved, stop on network error' contract the type documents does not hold under overlapping flushes.
confirmed.rule: plan D6 (offline queue: Saved/Shopping ops replay in order, idempotent)
fixes: Make flush non-re-entrant inside the actor. Minimal version in OfflineQueue.swift: add `private var flushing = false`, and at the top of `flush` do `guard !flushing else { return FlushResult(remaining: items.count) }; flushing = true; defer { flushing = false }`. Additionally (or alternatively) make each post-await mutation id-checked so a stale iteration can never remove the wrong element: replace `items.removeFirst()` with `if items.first?.id == item.id { items.removeFirst() }` and `items[0].attempts += 1` with `if let i = items.firstIndex(where: { $0.id == item.id }) { items[i].attempts += 1 }`. A tests-only reproduction: enqueue two ops, start two `flush` calls concurrently against an executor that suspends (e.g. `await Task.yield()`/continuation) before returning, and assert the executor saw both item ids exactly once and `items` is empty.

Make flush non-re-entrant and stop mutating by position. In OfflineQueue: add `private var isFlushing = false`; at the top of `flush`, `guard !isFlushing else { return FlushResult(remaining: items.count) }` (or await a stored in-flight Task and return its result), set `isFlushing = true` and `defer { isFlushing = false }`. Additionally, replace the positional mutations with id-based ones so a stale iteration can never remove or index the wrong element: `items.removeAll { $0.id == item.id }` on success/reject, and `if let i = items.firstIndex(where: { $0.id == item.id }) { items[i].attempts += 1 }` on transient failure. Add a test in SharingTests that starts two concurrent `flush` calls against a slow FakeExecutor with a two-item queue and asserts each item is executed exactly once and nothing remains.

confirmed.title: Any authenticated account can define or amend shared place data used by every other trip
confirmed.detail: app.places is a global cache readable by every authenticated user (migration 1 line 219-220: `create policy places_authenticated_read on app.places for select to authenticated using (true)`), and app.upsert_place is callable by any authenticated user with no trip membership check at all (it only calls `perform app.current_user_id()`). Two cross-tenant writes follow. (a) First-writer-wins with no validation against the provider: an attacker who registers ('apple_mapkit', <real Apple identifier>) with an arbitrary name and latitude/longitude before anyone else permanently binds that identifier for every trip; when a legitimate user's client later calls upsert_place with the real data, the `on conflict ... do update` never touches name/latitude/longitude, so the attacker's coordinates are returned and become the stop's place_id used in route computation. There is no admin/repair path. places.test.sql lines 53-55 confirms the second caller's coordinates (0,0) are ignored, which is the same mechanism in reverse. (b) The `coalesce(app.places.name_local, excluded.name_local)` / `coalesce(app.places.name_zh, excluded.name_zh)` fill-in lets any authenticated user (including a non-member or a Viewer of an unrelated trip) set the Chinese/local display name of any existing place whose value is still null; that text is then rendered inside other users' itineraries and Saved lists. Identifiers are discoverable because places is enumerable via the `using (true)` policy. This violates 「權限一律由服務端驗證」 for data that feeds other trips' route math.
confirmed.evidence:
on conflict (provider, provider_place_id) do update
    set name_local = coalesce(app.places.name_local, excluded.name_local),
        name_zh = coalesce(app.places.name_zh, excluded.name_zh)
  returning * into p;

fixes: Minimal server-side fix in a new migration replacing app.upsert_place: (a) drop the cross-tenant fill-in — on conflict do nothing (as in 20260924000002) and instead store name_zh/name_local overrides on the trip-scoped rows (stops / saved_places) or only allow the fill-in when the caller is a member of a trip that references the place (`exists (select 1 from app.stops s where s.place_id = app.places.id and app.trip_role_of(s.trip_id) is not null)`); (b) on conflict, if the incoming latitude/longitude differ from the stored row by more than a small tolerance (e.g. 100 m), raise a PLACE_CONFLICT error instead of silently returning the stored row, so a client that has the real MapKit data never adopts poisoned coordinates; (c) add `created_by uuid` to app.places for audit and an owner/service-role repair path. Longer term, resolve identity fields via the apple_maps_server provider in an Edge Function rather than trusting client-supplied coordinates.

In app.upsert_place: add `created_by uuid` to app.places and (a) restrict the coalesce fill-in of name_local/name_zh to callers who are the row's creator or a member of a trip that references the place (exists in app.stops / app.saved_places / app.shopping merchants where app.trip_role_of(trip_id) is not null); (b) on conflict, if the existing row's coordinates differ from the caller's by more than a small tolerance (e.g. ~100 m via earth-distance), do not silently return the existing row — raise 'PLACE_CONFLICT' (PT409) or insert a separate row keyed by (provider, provider_place_id, created_by) so one account's bad data cannot bind the identifier for everyone. Add a places.test.sql case asserting an outsider cannot fill name_zh on a place it does not use.

Minimal: in supabase/migrations (new migration) add `created_by uuid not null default app.current_user_id()` to app.places, and change upsert_place's `on conflict ... do update` to fill name_local/name_zh only when the caller may legitimately edit that row, e.g. `where app.places.created_by = app.current_user_id() or exists (select 1 from app.stops s where s.place_id = app.places.id and app.trip_role_of(s.trip_id) in ('owner','editor'))` (otherwise `do nothing` and return the existing row as migration 2 did). For the first-writer problem, add a server-side guard on conflict: if the incoming coordinates differ from the stored ones by more than a small threshold (e.g. > 500 m), do not silently return the stored row — raise `PLACE_MISMATCH` (PT409) so the client re-resolves and the row can be flagged for review, and provide an owner/service-role repair RPC. Alternatively, keep places purely as identity (provider, provider_place_id) and move name_zh/name_local overrides into trip-scoped columns on app.stops / app.saved_places so display text is never writable across tenants.

confirmed.title: commit_itinerary skips the STALE_REVISION check when p_expected_route_revision is NULL
confirmed.detail: The revision guard is a plain `<>` comparison. If the caller passes JSON null for p_expected_route_revision (PostgREST maps it to SQL NULL), `d.route_revision <> NULL` evaluates to NULL, the IF is not taken, and the commit proceeds to rewrite the whole day and soft-delete every stop not in the list, with no revision check at all. create_proposal is protected only by accident (the NOT NULL column on change_proposals.expected_route_revision makes the insert fail with 23502). Any editor-role client that sends null, e.g. a future optional field or a hand-crafted request, overwrites the formal itinerary silently, which is exactly what the revision check exists to prevent. The current Swift StopDraft/Params encode a non-optional Int, so the shipped app does not trigger it, but the rule is required to hold server-side.
confirmed.evidence:
if d.route_revision <> p_expected_route_revision then
    raise exception 'STALE_REVISION'
confirmed.rule: CLAUDE.md: 正式行程提交需檢查 revision，過期 proposal 不可靜默覆蓋

Apply the same `is distinct from` to create_proposal at 20260924000004_change_proposals.sql:81 and 20260924000008_ai_assistant.sql:52 for a clear error instead of the accidental 23502. Add a test case in supabase/tests/itinerary_revision.test.sql: `select tests.throws(format($$select app.commit_itinerary(%L, null, '[]')$$, :'day_id'), 'PT409', 'null revision rejected');`.

Optionally apply the same `is null or ... is distinct from` form to create_proposal (004:81, 008:52) so the rule does not depend on the column's NOT NULL constraint, and add a test in supabase/tests/itinerary_revision.test.sql: `select tests.throws(format($$select app.commit_itinerary(%L, null, '[]')$$, :'day_id'), 'PT409', 'null revision rejected');`.

confirmed.detail: mark_saved_added only moves saved -> added_to_itinerary; the soft-delete branch (new.deleted_at is not null) does nothing, so removing the stop via commit_itinerary leaves the Saved row hidden from the 'to add' list although the place is no longer on the itinerary. The row is not dismissed either, so save_place's place dedupe (`status <> 'dismissed'`, migration 6 lines 141-142) matches it and returns duplicate=true with the stale status: the user cannot get the place back into Saved for that trip. Scenario: save Onion (status saved) -> commit day with Onion (status added_to_itinerary, trigger) -> commit day without Onion (stop tombstoned, saved status unchanged) -> save_place(Onion) returns the added_to_itinerary row, no new entry.

confirmed.title: Account deletion is two non-atomic steps; prepare's irreversible effects survive a failed deleteUser
confirmed.detail: `prepare_account_deletion` hard-deletes the caller's solo trips, transfers shared trips to an heir (trips.owner_id and heir's trip_members.role = 'owner') and deletes their import_sessions, and only then is `auth.admin.deleteUser` called. If deleteUser fails (Auth API error, network, rate limit) the function returns 500 DELETE_FAILED, but the trips are already gone/transferred and nothing is rolled back. Concrete state after that path: the account still exists and can sign in; its solo trips and pasted import text are permanently deleted; each shared trip now has two members with role 'owner' (the old owner's trip_members row is only removed by the auth.users cascade, which never ran) while trips.owner_id points at the heir. The iOS client (Hardening.swift deleteAccount) surfaces DELETE_FAILED and keeps the session, so the user sees a working account with missing trips. The migration test only covers the happy path (prepare then `delete from auth.users`).
confirmed.rule: docs/planning/mvp-technical-plan.md §3.1 刪除策略; docs/acceptance/mvp-acceptance.md 刪除帳號
fixes: Make the whole deletion one transaction: extend app.prepare_account_deletion (or add app.delete_account(p_user_id)) to end with `delete from auth.users where id = p_user_id;` (service_role, security definer — exactly what the SQL test already does), so the trip transfers, anonymisation and the auth-user removal commit or roll back together; then have the Edge Function call only that RPC and drop the separate `auth.admin.deleteUser` step. If the Admin API must stay, at minimum (a) in prepare, delete or demote the leaving user's trip_members row for transferred trips so no dual-owner state exists, and (b) retry deleteUser a few times before returning DELETE_FAILED, and add a test asserting the partial-failure state.

Make the transfer and the user removal one transaction: extend `app.prepare_account_deletion` (security definer, service_role only) to end with `delete from auth.users where id = p_user_id;` (exactly what supabase/tests/deletion.test.sql:29-32 already does, so the cascades are known to work), rename it e.g. `app.delete_account`, and have the Edge Function call only that RPC, dropping the separate `auth.admin.deleteUser` step. If deleting auth.users via SQL is not wanted, the fallback is to keep the two steps but make prepare non-destructive until deleteUser succeeds (e.g. move the solo-trip and import_sessions hard-deletes into a second RPC run only after deleteUser returns OK, and rely on the cascade for the rest), plus add a test for the deleteUser-failure path.

Make the pre-step leave a self-consistent state and make the second step retry: (a) in app.prepare_account_deletion, after transferring each trip also `delete from app.trip_members where trip_id = t.id and user_id = p_user_id;` (or delete all of the user's memberships at the end) so a transferred trip never has two owners; (b) in delete-account/index.ts, retry `admin.auth.admin.deleteUser(userId)` a few times with backoff before returning DELETE_FAILED, and log the userId so it can be finished manually; (c) add a test asserting prepare is idempotent (second call returns transferred=0, deleted=0) and that no trip has two 'owner' members after prepare alone.

confirmed.title: No per-user rate limit or quota on the Claude-backed functions; any authenticated member can drive unbounded API spend
confirmed.detail: ask-trip accepts any number of POSTs from any active trip member and each call goes straight to `client.beta.messages.parse` with `max_tokens: 16000` on the default Opus model; parse-import likewise re-parses on every call (each import_session may hold 50,000 chars of raw_text, and a user can create unlimited sessions). Neither function nor any SQL function checks a per-user count, a cooldown, or an in-flight state before calling the provider (ai_messages is only written after the call; import_sessions.parse_status='parsing' is not checked before starting another parse). A single compromised or malicious account, or a client bug that retries in a loop, can exhaust the ANTHROPIC_API_KEY budget with no server-side cap. The gateway only verifies the JWT, which the app's own users hold.
fixes: Add a server-side per-user cap before each provider call. Minimal version: (1) ask-trip: after resolving userId and before line 129, use the admin client to count `ai_messages` rows for `user_id = userId` with `created_at > now() - interval '1 hour'` (and optionally `status`-agnostic), and return `json({ error: "RATE_LIMITED" }, 429)` when over a threshold (e.g. 30/hour); also insert the ai_messages row with status 'pending' BEFORE the call and update it after, so an in-flight request counts toward the cap. (2) parse-import: after loading the session, return 409 `PARSE_IN_PROGRESS` when `session.parse_status === 'parsing'` and `updated_at` is within the last few minutes; and count `import_sessions` rows for `created_by = uid` updated in the last hour (or add a small `app.ai_calls` ledger table written by both functions via service role) and return 429 when over a threshold. Optionally cap concurrent import sessions per user in `app.create_import`. A cleaner shared form is a `security definer` SQL function `app.reserve_ai_call(p_user_id uuid, p_kind text, p_limit int, p_window interval) returns boolean` that inserts into an `app.ai_calls` ledger and returns false when the window count is exceeded; both functions call it and return 429 on false.

Add a server-side gate before the provider call in both functions. ask-trip: after resolving userId (index.ts:39), run `admin.from("ai_messages").select("id", { count: "exact", head: true }).eq("user_id", userId).gte("created_at", new Date(Date.now() - 60*60*1000).toISOString())` and return json({ error: "RATE_LIMITED" }, 429) when count >= N (e.g. 30/hour); optionally also insert a 'pending' ai_messages row first and update it after, so in-flight calls count. parse-import: before `record("parsing", ...)` (index.ts:55), refuse with 409 when `session.parse_status === "parsing"` and `session.updated_at` is within the last few minutes, and refuse with 429 when the user has more than N import_sessions with parse_status in ('parsing','parsed','failed') updated in the last hour (count via admin client on import_sessions by created_by). Optionally make the 'pending'->'parsing' transition atomic in SQL (`update ... where parse_status <> 'parsing' returning id`) so concurrent requests cannot both start.

In ask-trip, before calling the provider, count app.ai_messages for (user_id, created_at > now() - interval '1 hour'/'1 day') with the admin client and return {error:"RATE_LIMITED"} 429 above a threshold (e.g. 20/hour, 100/day). In parse-import, reject when session.parse_status = 'parsing' and updated_at is within the last few minutes (409 IN_PROGRESS), and count import_sessions created by the user in the last day (or parse attempts) against a cap before record("parsing"). Also set a monthly spend limit on the Anthropic workspace as a backstop.

confirmed.title: parse-import holds the HTTP response for the whole Claude parse and does not guard against a concurrent re-parse; a client timeout produces a false failure and a duplicate parse
confirmed.detail: The function awaits `parseItinerary` (streamed from Claude, 16,000 max output tokens, the source comment says minutes at high effort) before answering, while the app already polls `parse_progress` separately. The iOS client (Backend.swift builds SupabaseClient with default options, i.e. URLSession.shared whose timeoutIntervalForRequest is 60 s) swallows the invoke error and reads the session (Import.swift lines 244-249); with the row still at 'parsing' ImportFlowView sets phase = .failed with the generic "暫時無法連線到解析服務" text while the server keeps parsing and later writes 'parsed'. Pressing 重試 starts a second invocation for the same import_id: there is no `parse_status = 'parsing'` check before `record("parsing")`, so both invocations run, both bill the API, and whichever finishes last overwrites parse_result. If the Edge Runtime kills the request on its wall-clock limit or a worker restart, nothing marks the session 'failed' (only the in-process catch does), so the row stays 'parsing' with no error until the user manually retries.
fixes: 1) Make the 'parsing' transition an atomic claim: add an RPC (service_role only) e.g. `app.claim_parse(p_import_id uuid) returns boolean` doing `update app.import_sessions set parse_status='parsing', parse_error=null, updated_at=now() where id=p_import_id and trip_id is null and (parse_status in ('pending','failed') or (parse_status='parsing' and updated_at < now() - interval '3 minutes')) returning true`; in parse-import/index.ts replace line 55 with this call and return `json({ error: "PARSE_IN_PROGRESS" }, 409)` when it returns false. The stale window lets a retry recover a row left at 'parsing' by a killed worker. 2) In ImportFlowView.parse(), on invoke error/timeout keep polling `service.session` until parse_status leaves 'parsing' (bounded, e.g. 3 min) before setting `.failed`, and only call parse() from `.task` when parseStatus is pending/failed (or 'parsing' older than the stale window), not for every non-parsed row.

Minimal fix in two parts:

(a) Server claim, supabase/functions/parse-import/index.ts: replace the unconditional `await record("parsing", ...)` at line 55 with an atomic claim RPC (new migration) such as
  update app.import_sessions set parse_status='parsing', parse_error=null, parse_progress=null, updated_at=now()
   where id = p_import_id and trip_id is null and (parse_status <> 'parsing' or updated_at < now() - interval '10 minutes')
  returning id;
and return `json({ error: "PARSE_IN_PROGRESS" }, 409)` when no row is returned. Then respond immediately after the claim (`return json({ status: "parsing" })`) and run the parse via `EdgeRuntime.waitUntil(...)` so the HTTP response no longer waits on Claude.

(b) Client, Packages/AppCore/Sources/AppCore/Import.swift `parse(importID:)` / Packages/AppCore/Sources/Features/ImportFlowView.swift `parse()`: after invoke returns (or throws), keep polling `session(importID:)` while `parseStatus == .parsing` (bounded, e.g. up to the runtime limit) and only set `.failed` when the row reports `.failed` or the poll deadline passes; treat a 409 PARSE_IN_PROGRESS from 重試 as "keep polling", not as a new failure.

1) parse-import/index.ts: after the trip_id check, add `if (session.parse_status === "parsing" && Date.now() - Date.parse(session.updated_at) < STALE_MS) return json({ status: "parsing" }, 202);` so a retry cannot start a second concurrent parse, and treat older 'parsing' rows as stale (retryable). 2) Return immediately after record("parsing") and run the parse in the background with `EdgeRuntime.waitUntil(run())` so the HTTP response is not held for the whole model call. 3) ImportFlowView.parse(): when service.parse returns a session still at .parsing (or invoke throws), keep polling service.session until status becomes .parsed/.failed (with a cap, e.g. 8 min) instead of setting phase = .failed; on cap expiry show failure and let 重試 go through the stale-reset path above.

confirmed.title: max_tokens / invalid_output branches are unreachable: SDK throws inside finalMessage() before stop_reason is checked
confirmed.detail: betaZodOutputFormat() installs a `parse` function, and in @anthropic-ai/sdk 0.128.0 the beta stream calls maybeParseBetaMessage() on every text block at `message_stop` (lib/BetaMessageStream.js:432) regardless of stop_reason. That parse does `zodObject.safeParse(JSON.parse(content))` and throws AnthropicError('Failed to parse structured output') when JSON.parse fails or Zod rejects. When the model hits max_tokens mid-JSON (the normal case for a long itinerary: the output is truncated JSON), or emits schema-invalid JSON, `await stream.finalMessage()` rejects, so the code never reaches `if (response.stop_reason === "max_tokens")` or the `invalid_output` return. The exception propagates to supabase/functions/parse-import/index.ts:83, which records `provider_error` instead of `max_tokens`/`invalid_output`, and to eval/run.ts:84, which records status "error" instead of "failed". Only the case with zero text blocks (e.g. max_tokens exhausted entirely during thinking) reaches those branches. The same pattern applies to ai/trip-assistant/src/ask.ts:30-51, where client.beta.messages.parse() calls parseBetaMessage() unconditionally (resources/beta/messages/messages.js:83). The PARSE_FAILED reason contract (plan §3.5) is therefore misreported for the truncation case; to get the intended reasons the request must use output_config.format without the SDK `parse` hook (or catch AnthropicError and inspect the raw message's stop_reason).
fixes: Send the JSON schema without the SDK `parse` hook and do the parsing after the stop_reason checks. In ai/itinerary-parse/src/parse.ts: `const { parse: _ignored, ...format } = betaZodOutputFormat(ParseResult);` and pass `output_config: { format, effort }`; after the refusal/max_tokens checks, replace the `response.parsed_output` lines with: `const text = response.content.find((b) => b.type === "text")?.text; let raw: unknown; try { raw = text ? JSON.parse(text) : null; } catch (e) { return { status: "failed", reason: "invalid_output", detail: String(e) }; } const check = raw ? ParseResult.safeParse(raw) : null;` (rest unchanged). Apply the same change to ai/trip-assistant/src/ask.ts, switching `client.beta.messages.parse(...)` to `client.beta.messages.create(...)` (keeping betas/output_config) and parsing the first text block after the stop_reason checks. Alternative smaller patch: wrap `await stream.finalMessage()` in try/catch for `Anthropic.AnthropicError` that is not an `Anthropic.APIError`, and return `{ status: "failed", reason: stream.currentMessage?.stop_reason === "max_tokens" ? "max_tokens" : "invalid_output", detail: err.message }`.

confirmed.title: prepare_account_deletion leaves the departing user as an active owner and deletes their import text before the auth user is removed
confirmed.detail: The function promotes the heir (`update app.trip_members set role = 'owner'`) and repoints `app.trips.owner_id`, but never updates or removes the departing user's own trip_members row, which stays `role = 'owner', status = 'active'`. It relies entirely on the later `auth.admin.deleteUser` cascading that row away. supabase/functions/delete-account/index.ts lines 29-33 calls deleteUser after the RPC has already committed and, on failure, returns 500 without any compensation. In that state (deleteUser fails: transient network/Auth error) the trip has two active owners: the old owner still passes `app.require_role(..., array['owner'])` for delete_trip, create_invite, remove_member and set_member_role, and can demote the heir to viewer (set_member_role only forbids p_role = 'owner' and self-targeting), leaving trips.owner_id pointing at a viewer. Re-running the function does not repair this because the loop is `where owner_id = p_user_id`, which no longer matches. In the same failed-delete case, lines 143/154 have already irreversibly deleted the user's import_sessions (pasted raw text) even though the account persists.
fixes: In app.prepare_account_deletion, inside the `else` branch after promoting the heir, mark the departing owner's membership inactive so they are no longer an active owner: `update app.trip_members set status = 'removed' where trip_id = t.id and user_id = p_user_id;` (or delete the row). Additionally, defer the irreversible personal-data step: either move `delete from app.import_sessions where created_by = p_user_id` (line 81) out of the RPC and rely on the created_by on-delete-cascade FK (import_sessions.sql:11), or have the Edge Function call deleteUser first only after a cheap precheck, and on deleteUser failure log/raise so the state can be retried. Optionally make the loop idempotent by also selecting trips where the user still holds an active owner membership (`or id in (select trip_id from app.trip_members where user_id = p_user_id and role = 'owner' and status = 'active')`).

In app.prepare_account_deletion (supabase/migrations/20260924000009_deletion.sql), after the loop add `update app.trip_members set status = 'removed' where user_id = p_user_id and status = 'active';` so the departing user atomically loses owner/member access in the same transaction as the ownership transfer (idempotent on re-run; the later auth cascade still removes the row). Optionally have delete-account/index.ts retry deleteUser once before returning DELETE_FAILED.

In the transfer branch of app.prepare_account_deletion (supabase/migrations/20260924000009_deletion.sql:73-78), add `update app.trip_members set status = 'removed' where trip_id = t.id and user_id = p_user_id;` (or `delete from app.trip_members where user_id = p_user_id;` after the loop) so the trip never has two active owners regardless of whether auth.admin.deleteUser succeeds. Optionally have delete-account call deleteUser first and run the RPC only when it succeeds, or log the failed-delete userId for manual cleanup.

confirmed.title: A late parse result overwrites a draft that was reset by update_import_text, attaching the old text's result to the new text
confirmed.detail: record_parse_result has no guard on the current parse_status or on which raw_text was parsed; it only checks `trip_id is null`. update_import_text (line 84-87) resets parse_status to 'pending' and raw_text to the edited text while the parse-import Edge Function for the previous text is still running. When that function finishes it calls record_parse_result('parsed', <result for OLD text>), which succeeds and sets parse_status='parsed' with a parse_result that does not correspond to raw_text. The user then sees, and can commit, a draft built from text they already replaced. parse-import/index.ts re-reads nothing before recording, so the DB is the only place this can be enforced.

     set parse_status = p_status, parse_result = p_result, parse_error = p_error,
         model = p_model, updated_at = now()
   where id = p_import_id and trip_id is null;
fixes: Make record_parse_result (and record_parse_progress) prove which text they belong to. Minimal: add `p_raw_text text` to app.record_parse_result and change the where clause to `where id = p_import_id and trip_id is null and raw_text = p_raw_text` (or compare md5(raw_text)); in parse-import/index.ts pass `p_raw_text: session.raw_text` in the record() rpc call. Alternatively add a `parse_generation int` column bumped by update_import_text, have the function read it with the session and pass it back, and guard `and parse_generation = p_generation`. Optionally, client-side, keep phase = .parsing (and keep polling) when the returned session is still `.parsing` instead of dropping to .failed.

Bind each parse result to the text it parsed. Minimal version without a schema change: add a p_raw_text_hash text parameter to app.record_parse_result (and app.record_parse_progress) and extend the WHERE to `and md5(raw_text) = p_raw_text_hash`; in supabase/functions/parse-import/index.ts compute the hash of session.raw_text read at line 35 and pass it in every record()/record_parse_progress call. Cleaner alternative: add `parse_revision int not null default 0` to app.import_sessions, increment it in update_import_text, have the Edge Function pass the revision it read, and guard `and parse_revision = p_revision` in both service-role functions. Update the function signatures in the revoke/grant lists (lines 157-171) and add a test in supabase/tests/imports.test.sql that update_import_text followed by a stale record_parse_result leaves parse_status='pending'.

Tag each parse with the text it belongs to: add `parse_version int not null default 1` to app.import_sessions, increment it in update_import_text, have parse-import read it with the session and pass it to record_parse_result / record_parse_progress, and change their WHERE to `where id = p_import_id and trip_id is null and parse_version = p_parse_version`. (Cheaper variant without a column: add `p_raw_text_md5 text` and `and md5(raw_text) = p_raw_text_md5`, with the function passing md5 of the raw_text it parsed.)

confirmed.title: Concurrency checks depend on a 0.5 s sleep to order two psql sessions and fail on a slow runner
confirmed.detail: Session A is started in the background and B is launched after `sleep 0.5`; the test asserts B gets STALE_REVISION and the surviving stop is 'from A'. If A's psql startup plus login takes longer than 0.5 s (cold CI runner), B acquires the day lock first, A is the one that fails, LABELS is 'from B' and the run exits non-zero although the server behaved correctly. The same pattern is used for the proposal race at line 125.
fixes:
Replace the fixed `sleep 0.5` with an explicit handshake so B only starts once A holds the lock. E.g. in session A's heredoc add a psql shell meta-command right after the locking call:

  select app.commit_itinerary('$DAY_ID', 0, '[{"raw_label":"from A"}]');
  \! touch "$WORK/a.locked"
  select pg_sleep(1.5);

and in the script replace `sleep 0.5` with:

  until [[ -f "$WORK/a.locked" ]]; do sleep 0.05; done

(or poll `select count(*) from pg_stat_activity where datname='t_concurrency' and wait_event='PgSleep'` until it is 1). Apply the same change to the proposal race at run.sh:116-125 (touch "$WORK/pa.locked" after the confirm_proposal call). Optionally also increase pg_sleep or drop it entirely once the handshake exists, since B blocking on the row lock no longer depends on the sleep window.

Replace the fixed `sleep 0.5` (lines 75 and 125) with a readiness poll that waits until session A actually holds the day row lock before starting B, e.g.:

wait_for_day_lock() {  # $1=db $2=day id
  for _ in $(seq 1 100); do
    [[ -z "$("${PSQL[@]}" -d "$1" -At -c "select 1 from app.trip_days where id='$2' for update skip locked")" ]] && return 0
    sleep 0.1
  done
  echo "timed out waiting for session A to take the day lock"; return 1
}
wait_for_day_lock t_concurrency "$DAY_ID"        # instead of sleep 0.5 at line 75
wait_for_day_lock t_proposal_race "$RACE_DAY"     # instead of sleep 0.5 at line 125

(`for update skip locked` returns no row once A holds the lock and never blocks, so B is only launched after A is guaranteed to be first.)

confirmed.title: Unscoped, unlimited reads of purchase_events/saved_interests/merchant_candidates are capped by PostgREST max_rows, so shopping status can be wrong
confirmed.detail: These three queries carry no trip filter and no `.limit()`; RLS returns rows from every trip the caller belongs to and PostgREST truncates the result at `max_rows = 1000` (supabase/config.toml line 18). purchase_events is ordered by id ascending and the code derives an item's status from `.at(-1)` of the filtered rows, so once the caller's visible purchase events exceed 1000 the newest events are the ones dropped: an item whose latest event is 'purchased' is reported as "unscheduled"/"scheduled", and an item whose latest event is 'undone' (with an older 'purchased' still inside the first 1000) is reported as "purchased". saved_interests (`interested` names) and merchant_candidates (possible sellers) are truncated the same way. The model then answers from a wrong context with no indication anything was cut. Trigger: an active user in several trips with >1000 purchase events / interests overall.

confirmed.title: Empty or whitespace-only place_name (and empty source_excerpt) pass validation as a clean stop
confirmed.detail: The presence checks are substring tests, and `squash("")` / `squash("   ")` is the empty string, which `String.prototype.includes` always accepts. A model draft with `place_name: ""` or `"   "` therefore raises no issue, keeps `needs_confirmation: []`, and `isCleanStop()` returns true because `"" !== null`, so the app sends the stop straight to the Place lookup with a blank name (verified by running validateDraft: `{"place_name":""} issues=[] clean=true`). Likewise `source_excerpt: ""` yields zero issues and confidence stays "high", so the side-by-side review has nothing to show and the fabricated-excerpt downgrade is bypassed. The schema (`z.string().nullable()`) does not reject empty strings either. This defeats the validator's purpose that anything unverifiable is downgraded to needs-confirmation.

confirmed.title: Trip-assistant scorer has no negative test; dry-run only feeds it answers built to pass
confirmed.detail: `reference()` constructs the answer directly from the expectations (same cannot_determine, exactly the must_cite ids, exactly the expected proposal), so the dry-run exercises only the pass path. test/validate.test.ts never imports eval/score.ts, so nothing checks that scoreCase() fails a wrong cannot_determine, a missing citation, an unexpected proposal, or a forbidden phrase. Optionally also assert the reference answer passes to keep the positive path covered.

confirmed.screen: 全 App 錯誤訊息列

confirmed.screen: Today / Trip 時間軸 / Map（頁尾）
confirmed.issue: A developer-facing revision number ('資料版本 r12') is rendered as caption2 tertiary/secondary text at the bottom of three user screens (TodayView line 146, TripDetailView line 222, TripMapView line 61). It is the lightest text style in the app and carries no user meaning; on Map it is stacked under the layer picker inside the material bar.
confirmed.suggestion: Remove the 資料版本 row from Today, Trip detail and Map; expose the revision only in DebugMenuView (or TelemetryView). Keep the 離線資料 label on Today since it is actionable.

confirmed.issue: The day header VStack uses three sizes on three lines: .headline trip name, .subheadline secondary '第 N 天 · date', and .caption2 tertiary '首爾時間'. The third line is caption2 + tertiary, the hardest-to-read combination on a plain list background, and the trip name repeats the trip picker already in the toolbar.
confirmed.suggestion: Collapse to two lines: '第 N 天 · 2026-09-26' (.headline) and '首爾時間' appended to the same subheadline line as '… · 首爾時間' in .secondary; drop the caption2/tertiary line. Show the trip name only when store.trips.count > 1 (it is then also in the picker) or drop it.

confirmed.issue: Under the header 今天可買 a row '已買 3／10' shows the whole-trip purchase count, which reads as today's count, and duplicates the ProgressView already at the top of the Shopping tab.
confirmed.suggestion: Drop this LabeledContent row from Today (progress lives in the Shopping tab), or if kept, relabel it '全程已買' so the number matches its section.

confirmed.issue: The trip row subtitle prints the raw IANA identifier ('2026-09-25 – 2026-09-30 · Asia/Seoul'); every other screen shows the localized name via TripTimeZones.displayName. The identifier is English, long, and can truncate the dates at larger type.
confirmed.suggestion: Use TripTimeZones.displayName(trip.timeZone) or omit the time zone from the list row entirely (it is per-day anyway and shown in each day header); keep just the date range.

confirmed.screen: Trip 時間軸 / Today（路段列）
confirmed.issue: LegRow indents with a hard-coded 52pt leading padding to line up under the stop name, assuming the time column is ~40pt wide. With larger Dynamic Type the '10:30' column widens and the leg text no longer aligns; in TodayView the time column has no fixed width at all, so alignment differs between the two screens.
confirmed.suggestion: Remove .padding(.leading, 52) and let the icon lead the row, or move LegRow inside StopRow's trailing VStack so it inherits the same column without a magic number.

confirmed.issue: A '類型: 彈性' row appears on every stop even though 彈性 is the default and fixed stops are already marked by the lock icon in the list; it is one more line in a header block that already has name, address, 時間, 停留 and 未定位.
confirmed.suggestion: Show the row only when stop.fixed is true (e.g. Label("固定行程", systemImage: "lock.fill")) and drop it for flexible stops.
confirmed.evidence: LabeledContent("類型", value: stop.fixed ? "固定" : "彈性")

confirmed.issue: The category is rendered as a caption capsule (the only pill in the app) on every row; when the segmented filter is set to 吃/買/咖啡/景點 the capsule repeats the active filter on each row.
confirmed.suggestion: Delete the capsule and its padding/background; fold the category into the existing status caption line ('美食 · 未定位，不計入路線') as plain .caption/.secondary text, and omit it when filter != .all.

confirmed.issue: Fixed stops on the map are marked with the 🔒 emoji, the only emoji in the UI; it renders in full colour, ignores .foregroundStyle(.white) and looks different from the SF Symbol lock.fill used on Today and Trip rows.
confirmed.suggestion: Replace the emoji with Image(systemName: "lock.fill").font(.caption).foregroundStyle(.white) so the fixed marker matches the list rows (the marker itself stays).

confirmed.screen: 給司機看（TaxiCard 中文對照）

confirmed.issue: Two stacked cards on one screen use different corner radii (20 and 16) and two different fills (.yellow.opacity(0.25) and .quaternary.opacity(0.5)); the same yellow tint is used for the offline warning banner in RootView, so the driver card borrows a warning colour.

confirmed.issue: The quoted source excerpt is printed under every item, including the auto-handled ones inside the DisclosureGroup, adding a caption line to items that need no decision.
confirmed.suggestion: Show the excerpt only when item.stop.needsConfirmation is non-empty (the user needs context to decide); hide it for auto-decided items.

confirmed.issue: Elapsed time is shown as '1:05' with no unit and the line uses the katakana middle dot '・' as a separator, while every other screen uses '·' with spaces; line 455 repeats the '・'.

confirmed.evidence: Text("已經過 \(seconds / 60):\(String(format: "%02d", seconds % 60))・長行程約需 1～2 分鐘")

confirmed.issue: The auto-decision note uses 'wand.and.stars' in accent colour, while the AI is represented by 'sparkles' in three other places (AI 助手 button, proposal Label, ProposalReview banner).

confirmed.issue: The chosen candidate is shown as LabeledContent with the place name as the label and the address as the trailing value, so a long name and a long address fight for one line and both truncate; the search results just below use a VStack of name + caption address.
confirmed.suggestion: Render the chosen candidate with the same VStack (Text(name) / Text(address).font(.caption).foregroundStyle(.secondary)) used for the results so the two states look identical.

confirmed.issue: A 我的顯示名稱 text field + 儲存 row is repeated on the Members screen although the identical control exists under 設定 → 顯示名稱 (AccountView), so the name can be edited from two places with two different footers.
